title: The Seat I Was Saving
scene: You save a train seat for a friend who is supposed to get on at the next station. When your friend misses the train, you have to quietly return the seat to public use while the person you turned away is still standing nearby.
sceneJa: 電車で次の駅から乗る友人のために席を取っておく。ところが友人は乗り遅れ、さっき席を断った相手がまだ近くにいる中で、何事もなかったように席を空けることになる。

chunks.en: I got on a fairly crowded train
chunks.ja: そこそこ混んだ電車に乗り

chunks.en: and was lucky enough to find
chunks.ja: 運よく見つけました

chunks.en: an empty seat by the window.
chunks.ja: 窓際の空席を
友人は乗ってくる予定でした
次の駅から

chunks.en: so I put my small bag beside me
chunks.ja: そこで隣に小さなバッグを置き

chunks.en: to save the seat for him.
chunks.ja: 彼のために席を取っておきました
次の駅で
何人かが乗ってきて
一人の男性がまっすぐ見ました
空いている席を
私はバッグを少し動かし

chunks.en: and said, ‘Sorry, my friend is getting on here,’
chunks.ja: 『すみません、ここで友人が乗ってくるんです』と言いました
まるで〜な人のような自信をもって
確かな情報を持っている
ドアが閉まりました

chunks.en: but my friend did not appear,
chunks.ja: しかし友人は現れず
そこでスマホを確認すると

chunks.en: and found a new message from him.
chunks.ja: 彼から新しいメッセージが届いていました
彼は電車に乗り遅れていて

chunks.en: and told me to go ahead
chunks.ja: 先に行ってほしいと言いました
彼を待たずに
私はすぐにバッグをどかし

chunks.en: and tried to look as though
chunks.ja: 〜であるかのように見せようとしました

chunks.en: the seat had always been available
chunks.ja: その席がずっと空いていた
一般の人に対して
残念ながら

chunks.en: the man from earlier was still standing nearby
chunks.ja: さっきの男性はまだ近くに立っていて
明らかに見届けていました
この一連の運用手続きをすべて

chunks.en: I gave him a small apologetic smile
chunks.ja: 私は小さく申し訳なさそうに笑い
席を指し示しました
すると彼はそれを受け入れ
特に表情を変えずに

chunks.en: For the rest of the journey,
chunks.ja: その後の移動中

chunks.en: I looked out of the window
chunks.ja: 私は窓の外を眺めました
いつになく集中して
特に見るものはありませんでした
でもその時点では
景色のほうがずっと扱いやすくなっていました
アイコンタクトよりも

questions.question: Which boundary is most natural?
options: I tried to look as though / the seat had always been available / to the general public
I tried / to look as / though the seat had always / been available
I tried to look / as though the seat / had always been / available to the general public
questions.explanation: ‘I tried to look as though’ introduces the appearance the speaker wanted to create, followed by the imagined situation and then who the seat was available to.

questions.question: What does ‘go ahead without him’ mean here?
options: Leave the train and wait for him
Continue the journey without waiting for him
questions.explanation: ‘Go ahead without someone’ means to continue rather than wait for that person.

questions.question: Why is the final line funny?
options: The speaker genuinely prefers scenery to people
The speaker is so embarrassed that looking outside feels easier than making eye contact
The man has asked the speaker to look outside
questions.explanation: The speaker describes ordinary embarrassment in an unusually calm, practical way: scenery has become the easier option.

speak: Start confident and helpful. Give ‘with the confidence of someone / who had reliable information’ a lightly self-aware tone. Let the awkwardness build after the message arrives, but keep the delivery restrained. Pause before the final sentence and read it as a calm observation rather than a punchline.
review: Today’s flow: helpful plan → public commitment → plan fails → awkward reversal → quiet avoidance. Useful chunks include ‘with the confidence of someone who ...’, ‘go ahead without ...’, and ‘as though ... had always been ...’.
